newsitem.title: UK: Scot Power sees benefit from Southern Water.
newsitem.headline: Scot Power sees benefit from Southern Water.

text.p: British multi-utility Scottish Power Plc said on Wednesday that it had put plans in place to improve pre-tax profits at its Southern Water unit by 52 million pounds a year with total job losses of 2,050.

It said pre-tax profits after restructuring costs were 167 million pounds ($278.6 million), up 31 percent from a year ago and paid out an interim dividend of 6.17 pence and raised its full year dividend forecast to 18.5 pence, an increase of 19 percent.

Scottish Power said it also expected to release cash of some 100 million pounds at Southern Water, the water and sewerage firm it bought for 1.68 billion pounds in August after a battle with rivals Southern Electric.
It made a 21.2 million pound restructuring charge for costs of integrating Southern Water.
Scottish Power said of the total 2,050 job losses seen, 710 would be from Southern Water by March 1999 while the remainder would come as a result of disposals and outsourcing.

Scottish Power Chairman Murray Stuart said the raised dividend forecast was as a result of the better-than-expected position at Southern Water. He said the second half of the year had begun satisfactorily for the group, which aims with its acquisitions of Southern Water and of electricity supplier Manweb, in 1995, to become a leading multi-utility in electricity, gas, water and telecommunications. ($1=.5995 Pound)
